cue_frames.caption_text: From Records, open Manage and select Report exports.
This area defines a repeatable output file: its columns, format and scope.
The page also explains that exports can be attached to a Workflow
step or placed on a schedule.
This lesson configures and checks the file locally; it does not send an email
or upload anything to an outside agency.
Select New export to prepare a separate training-record handoff.
Enter a meaningful Export name and a stable Key.
The example is Training record handoff, with an academy training handoff key.
The help requires lower-case letters, digits and hyphens, and
explains that a Workflow step or agency import may rely on this key.
Keep that relationship in mind before changing names in a live integration.
Add a description of exactly what this file is intended to contain.
Here the description explicitly limits the exercise to fictional
training-record identity, state and dates.
Use C S V as the Format, and choose the window scope for finalized records.
Check Training under Record definitions.
The help says that leaving every definition unchecked would export
all definitions, so select the intended scope deliberately.
For File name, enter the template token followed by the date token, as shown.
Keep the comma Delimiter, include a header row, and leave Enabled checked.
These settings define the file layout that the receiving
process will need to recognize.
Review Columns rather than accepting an unnecessarily broad output.
Select Record number, Record type, State, Duration in minutes, Finalized
in U T C, and Course from records.
The screenshot shows those six checks.
Other identity, participant and incident fields remain unselected in this example.
Choose the smallest useful set for your actual handoff and agree
its meaning with the recipient.
A consistent set of fields makes repeated exports easier to compare and import.
Scroll through the narrative and restricted sections before saving.
This exercise leaves all their column checkboxes unselected.
It also leaves Include narrative and personal detail, Include
restricted sections, and the acknowledgement about sending that
content outside Resgrid unchecked.
These are separate controls beneath the column catalog.
Review them together with the selected columns and the intended
Workflow destination when planning an actual integration.
Our local file contains none of those narrative or restricted fields.
For the first test, use No schedule and set Window to thirty days.
The help explains that zero instead uses the schedule period ending at the run.
Select Save after reviewing the prepared settings.
The saved template can be reopened with the same format, Training
selection and thirty-day window.
The Report exports index confirms The export was saved and lists
the window scope with No schedule.
Saving the template establishes the configuration; it does not
prove that the resulting file contains the expected records.
Open Runs for the template, then select Run now.
The page says this renders the export for checking before an agency sees it, and
audits every included record as an export.
The completed run shows a Manual trigger, two records, three hundred sixteen
bytes, a checksum and a Download link.
Download the file and compare its headers and rows with the intended handoff.
The retained exercise file has the six selected headers and two training
records, including one amended record in this finalized-record window.
Return to Edit and change Schedule to Daily.
Set Hour to six in department local time and keep the thirty-day window.
The form also contains weekday and day-of-month controls for
other schedule choices, but this exercise saves the Daily choice.
Review the hour and window together, then select Save.
Changing a schedule is a configuration step; the next screen will
confirm the stored next-run time.
We do not claim that an automatic run has already occurred.
After saving, Next run shows November third at six in the morning.
The index independently shows Daily and the same next-run value.
That is the saved scheduling result for this dated training exercise.
To leave the department without an active timer, reopen the template, choose
No schedule, and select Save again.
Reopening now shows No schedule with a dash for Next run.
Verify that stored result instead of assuming an unsaved
selection stopped the schedule.
Use the same configuration and checking process across department types.
Search-and-rescue teams, security companies, wildland contractors and
industrial emergency teams can standardize their permitted record handoffs.
Community paramedicine and mental health response teams can define an
appropriate coordination or training export, as can fire and E M S departments.
Start with the right definition and columns, check a manual file, and verify
the schedule before relying on it.
Delivery through a Workflow is a separate operation that must be configured and
tested for the intended recipient.
